target_customer: Law firms that want private AI trained on their own matters for timekeeping, intake, research, discovery and drafting
problem: Off-the-shelf legal AI hallucinates citations and cannot be deployed inside a firm's confidential environment. Firms lose billable time and lack monitoring of matters.
business_model: Custom B2B deployments sold to law firms via sales calls (pricing not public)
product_category: Private legal AI systems with a grounding and citation verification engine

founders.name: Michael Marcotte
education: Stanford, BS Mathematics and MS Computer Science
founders.background_notes: YC page: AI research at NVIDIA, built production agents for hardware debugging and formal verification.

founders.name: Peyton Marcotte
previous_startups: PMARC, astronaut exercise equipment (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page: PMARC supported by NASA, Brown University and 1517 Fund grants.

competitors.name: Harvey
competitors.what: Leading legal AI platform, runs in vendor cloud
competitors.traction_then: contracted by large firms per Sacra
competitors.funding_then: large venture funding, figures not verified here

competitors.name: Legora
competitors.what: Enterprise legal AI challenger to Harvey
competitors.traction_then: firms contract both Harvey and Legora per Sacra

competitors.name: ibl.ai
competitors.what: Self-hosted legal AI sold as a Harvey alternative

technical_complexity.rationale: Private deployment, per-firm fine tuning and a verification layer against primary sources are demanding but built on existing models and tooling.

defensibility.rationale: Per-firm trained systems and private deployment add some lock-in, but well funded legal AI vendors compete for the same firms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action aimed at Perceptron found as of the sources reviewed.

market_need_then: Sacra reports firms disqualify vendors if data leaves their environment or trains shared models, supporting demand for private deployments.

branding.domain_note: Uses perceptronml.com, a name plus ML suffix .com.
branding.community_and_virality: Artificial Lawyer covered its YC Summer 2026 acceptance; no other brand press found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is a general machine learning term shared with at least two other companies called Perceptron, which confuses search results.

outcome_analysis: Perceptron ML is an active Summer 2026 company with a two person team and no exit. Its private deployment angle addresses a documented law firm security requirement, but Harvey and Legora are well funded and entrenched. No verified funding or traction data exists, so its outcome is unknown.
notes: Unverified funding: CB Insights lists a $500K convertible note with YC; Startup Seeker says undisclosed. Single aggregator, so no round recorded. An Extruct page describes a different product named notyfi under the same name and was ignored. Perceptron is also the name of two unrelated companies. Competitor source dates are the year only. Completeness pass: a $500K convertible note is recorded from CB Insights alone, undated. FundedIQ lists $130K pre-seed June 2026 and Dealroom $125K seed, which conflict. Press about a $6.5M Perceptron round concerns a different company.
